objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a patient presenting with sudden, unilateral loss of vision.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: About 30 minutes ago, I suddenly lost vision in my right eye while I was watching TV. It was painless, and my left eye feels normal.
How would you describe the vision in your right eye right now - is it completely black/dark, more like a gray curtain or veil coming down, or has the vision returned to normal?
Patient: It’s not completely black—more like a gray curtain or veil has come down over my right eye, and it hasn’t returned to normal yet. It’s still painless.
Have you noticed any flashes of light (like lightning bolts or camera flashes) in that eye before or during the episode, or an increase in floaters (dark spots or cobwebs drifting in your vision)?
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any flashes of light, and I don’t think I saw an increase in floaters or dark spots during it.
Do you have any history of an irregular heartbeat (such as atrial fibrillation), heart valve disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol?

Patient: Yes, I have high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes, and I also have coronary artery disease. I don’t know about any irregular heartbeat, and I’ve not always taken my medications like I’m supposed to.
Do you have any other symptoms right now, such as weakness or numbness on one side of your body, difficulty speaking, facial drooping, dizziness, or a severe headache?
Patient: No, I don’t have any weakness or numbness on one side, my speech feels normal, and I haven’t noticed facial drooping. I’m not dizzy and I don’t have a severe headache.
How old are you, and have you had any similar episodes of vision loss in either eye before today?
Patient: I’m 60 years old, and I haven’t had any similar episodes of vision loss in either eye before today.
Is the vision loss in your right eye affecting the entire visual field equally, or is it primarily the top half or bottom half of your vision that is obscured?
Patient: I think it affects most of the view evenly—like a gray veil covering a large part of my right visual field, not just the top or bottom.

When you cover your left eye and look at me with just your right eye, can you see my face clearly, or can you only see light/shadows, or is it completely dark?

Also, do you have any new headache, tenderness over your temples, or jaw pain when chewing?

When I cover my left eye, I can see only a gray veil over your face, not completely dark, and I can make out light and some shapes. I don’t have any new headache, temple tenderness, or jaw pain when chewing.

Have you noticed any change in the vision loss since it started 30 minutes ago—has it gotten better, worse, or stayed the same? Also, do you smoke or have you ever been told you have carotid artery disease or narrowing?

Patient: It seems about the same as when it started—maybe a tiny bit worse, but mostly it’s stayed the same, and I do smoke about 10 cigarettes a day. I haven’t been told I have carotid artery disease or narrowing.
[DDX] Central Retinal Artery Occlusion, Retinal Detachment, Central Retinal Vein Occlusion, Amaurosis Fugax (prolonged/infarcted), Branch Retinal Artery Occlusion
